key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search identified 58 CuI-based ternary compounds as promising p-type transparent conductors, and showed that p-type transparent conductivity can arise beyond traditional delafossite rules, including tetrahedrally coordinated halide systems.
engineering_relevance: These results expand the design space for transparent electrodes and tandem photovoltaics by providing a computationally screened set of candidate p-type TCMs, including 20 intrinsically hole-doped semiconductors.
method: Minima hopping structure search over Cu–I-based ternary X–Cu–I compounds
Density functional theory filtering for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass
Re-analysis of valence-band chemical modulation descriptors to generalize design rules
evidence_signal: The study reports 58 candidate p-type TCMs, 49 of them previously unreported, with 20 degenerate semiconductors and a highlighted example Cu2FI2 showing a 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m0 hole effective mass.
watch_item: The candidates are computational predictions, so experimental synthesis, phase stability under real conditions, and carrier performance still need validation.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
